title: Entitlement Evaluator + Runtime Gateway Middleware for Cross-Plane Authorization
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Implement a horizontally-scalable Entitlement Evaluator service paired with lightweight runtime gateway middleware that enforces RBAC v2 decisions for API, runtime, and Console traffic. This ticket covers the evaluation API contract, an in-process/sidecar middleware shim for low-latency checks, audit appenders for high-fidelity logging, and SSO/SAML mapping hooks for admin roles. Goals: provide consistent allow/deny semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; keep p99 check latency <5ms for policy-cache hits; ensure every authorization event emits an auditable record to the audit pipeline; enable feature flags for progressive rollout and safe fallback policies.
motivation_and_tradeoffs: We iterate on a split architecture: centralized evaluator for complex policy logic + local gateway middleware for fast path enforcement. Trade-offs: central evaluator gives expressive policies and easier updates but adds network latency; local middleware with cached decisions reduces latency but requires strong invalidation strategies. We choose a hybrid approach: synchronous queries to evaluator for cache miss/critical admin ops, cached positive/negative decisions (TTL + invalidation on policy push) for typical request flows, and a safe default-deny for unknown states. This balances operational simplicity, security posture, and performance.
design_summary: - API: /v1/decide POST accepts attributes {subject, resource, action, context} and returns {decision: allow|deny|conditional, reasons[], obligations[]}. - Local middleware: fast cache lookup keyed by hashed attribute tuple + bounded in-memory store with LRU + per-tenant namespaces. - Auditing: every decision emits an envelope to the 'rbac-audit' Kafka topic with immutable metadata (request_id, actor_id, policy_version, decision, timestamp, trace_id). - SSO/SAML: evaluator consumes mapped SAML assertions (roles, groups) and provides canonical principal attributes used in policy evaluation. - Admin controls: Console guard middleware consults evaluator for admin-only flows and surfaces reason strings for diagnostics in session logs (only to authorized operators).
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator API defined and documented (OpenAPI spec checked in to rbac-v2/docs)
Middleware implemented as a lightweight Go module + node shim used in API gateway with CI tests
Cache TTL and invalidation tested under policy push scenarios with no stale allow after 2s window
End-to-end audit events appear in test Kafka cluster and are queryable in staging audit UI
SAML role mapping path exercised in integration test against dev IdP
Performance: cache hit p99 < 5ms, cache miss p99 < 25ms in synthetic load
implementation_notes: - Use protobuf for evaluator internal contract and gRPC for high-throughput private deployments; REST/JSON facade for hosted API consumers. - Cache keys must include policy_version and tenant_id to avoid cross-tenant leakage. - On policy publish, publish an invalidation event to 'rbac-cache-control' topic and include vector clock metadata. - Telemetry: rbac.v2.evaluator.latency_ms, rbac.v2.cache.hit_ratio, rbac.v2.audit.emitted_count. - Rollout strategy: start with canary on staging-console and 10% of hosted API traffic, monitor errors/latency, then ramp to 50% before full rollout. - Fallbacks: config flag allow_on_error=false by default; ops can enable allow_on_error=true for limited low-impact workloads via release toggles.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stale cache allowing unauthorized access. Mitigation: short default TTL (1s), strict invalidation on policy pushes, and conservative default-deny. Risk: audit volume explosion. Mitigation: batching for audit pipeline and sampling for low-risk read-only operations while preserving full logging for admin/admin-sso flows. Risk: SSO mapping discrepancies. Mitigation: canonicalization layer and integration tests against IdP assertion samples.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge evaluator service and middleware behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging and enable 5% traffic via gateway routing. 3) Run 48h smoke test, validate metrics and audits. 4) Enable SAML mapping tests with staging IdP. 5) Ramp to 25% then 100% while monitoring alerts (authorization-fail-rate, rbac-audit-errors). 6) Post-deploy security review and incident runbook update.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy permutations, fuzz tests for attribute inputs, integration tests that spin up evaluator+middleware+staging-kafka, chaos test that simulates evaluator latency to validate local-cache behavior, end-to-end SAML assertion replay tests, and automated red-team scenario that attempts privilege escalation via rapid role changes.
